01 — The Problem

The problem & the prodrome

Migraine is one of the most disabling neurological conditions worldwide. Yet most interventions begin after pain has already started — when the window for early action has already closed.

Before a migraine headache begins, many people experience a prodrome phase — subtle physiological changes that may occur hours or even days before pain onset, including changes in heart rate variability, body temperature, sleep patterns, and stress levels.

01

Normal

Baseline physiological state.

02

Prodrome

Subtle physiological changes — often unrecognized.

03

Headache

Pain onset — intervention window missed.

Physiological changes may occur before pain, but users often don't recognize or act on them. The challenge is not the absence of signals — it's the absence of awareness and interpretation.

02 — The Solution

The NeuroBand solution

NeuroBand is a complete system — from raw physiological signals to personalized risk insight. The goal is not a single universal migraine threshold, but individualized pattern recognition unique to each user. Each user's baseline is unique, and so is their early warning system.

03 — The Sensors

Four signals, one bracelet

NeuroBand integrates multiple physiological sensors into a single wearable bracelet, each capturing a different dimension of the body's pre-symptomatic state.

♥

Heart Rate / HRV

Reflects autonomic nervous system activity — a potential early indicator of neurological stress and migraine prodrome.

≈

Accelerometer / Movement

Movement and activity patterns help contextualize physiological data and detect behavioral changes preceding an episode.

Zz

Sleep Monitoring

Sleep quality and duration are well-documented migraine triggers. Continuous tracking enables correlation with attack patterns.

°T

Temperature

Peripheral temperature changes may signal autonomic shifts associated with the pre-headache phase.

07 — Scientific Evidence Review

Does the science back this up?

We reviewed the latest peer-reviewed and preprint research testing whether AI can actually forecast migraine from real-world data. Three independent 2025–26 studies stood out.

1

Can Wearables Forecast a Migraine Attack?

Faisal et al., The Journal of Headache and Pain, Mar 2026
0.84 AUC
Time-pattern model vs. 50% baseline

146 people with migraine used a headache diary app plus a wearable sensor for up to 3 months. Only a time-pattern AI (trained on sequences of days) clearly beat a coin-flip at predicting next-day headache — simple and general-purpose models barely did.

2

Does "Your Own Data" Predict Better Than Averages?

Tsai et al., Headache: J. of Head and Face Pain, Jul 2026
0.83 vs 0.63
Personalized vs. generalized AUC

25 people with migraine kept a digital headache diary for 3 months. A model trained only on each person's own patterns clearly outperformed a "one-size-fits-all" model at predicting whether today's migraine persists into tomorrow.

3

Can Smartwatches Predict Migraine Overnight?

Tomalin et al., Research Square preprint, Dec 2025
80% vs 0%
Episodic vs. chronic patients beating chance

10 people wore a smartwatch overnight, tracking skin response, heart-rhythm variability, breathing and sleep — no diary needed. A personal AI model worked far better for episodic migraine than for near-daily chronic migraine.

Three lessons emerge: prediction is about patterns over time, not one magic signal; personalized models beat generalized ones; and multimodal signals improve individualized prediction — the direction NeuroBand is built on.

These are early-stage findings, not clinical validation of NeuroBand itself. Sample sizes are small and results vary by individual.
